title: Fugaro setup --events
description: One line of the newline-delimited feed `fugaro setup --events --json` and `fugaro update --events --json` write (docs/console-improvements ST2, D2904): the run `--json` prints as one document, written as one event per line so a surface that drives the CLI draws each stage as it settles instead of holding the whole document before it can draw anything — the console's first-run wizard spawns `setup --plan-only --answers-file - --events --json` and renders the lines as they arrive. The schema is of ONE LINE and not of the feed: a reader validates each line as it reads it, and the feed is the lines in order. The kinds are the console's own closed set (SETUP_EVENT_TYPES, console/src/shared/new-ops.ts, which holds the shape this file and the golden `internal/cli/testdata/setup_events.golden.ndjson` are the authority for): `step` is the run reaching a stage and starting to work on it, `stage` is one stage it settled with the very members the document's `stages` element carries, `left_for_you` is one thing only the user can do — with the step's own line to run, because a surface reading this has no terminal to hand it to — `notice` is one line the run reported outside its stages (a step after the stage loop, an admit pattern the reader could not list: R12, R19) and the last line is `done` with the run's own exit code — including a run that ends with steps left for the user, which is exit 1 and not a failure — or `error` for the run that stopped: the stage it stopped at with the CLI's sentence and fix, or, where it refused before any stage, the refusal itself with `stage` empty. A feed with no last line is an interrupted read, which is the failure a consumer must handle either way — a killed child, a truncated pipe, a cap reached — and no `version` member is carried to answer it: the members here are the contract's own (a version is one the console's copy holds no place for), and a feed's shape changes only by adding a member within it. Members are only ever added for that reason, and no object here is closed: additionalProperties is left true everywhere, because a consumer that refused a member this schema does not know would refuse a newer CLI's feed. Nothing here confirms a step: `--json` confirms none (unconfirmedWhy, internal/cli/init.go), so every step that needs a confirmation arrives as a `left_for_you` line exactly as it is left without the flag, and no member of this feed is a consent — a wizard's yes is its owner's go to run the CLI in their own terminal, never a word the CLI reads.

step.description: The run reaching a stage and starting to work on it: the moment a person watching sees a line go up for it, and the one fact a reader of the results cannot place afterwards, because a stage's check and plan are seconds and the apply behind them is minutes. One is written per stage the run works on, and the `stage` line for the same stage follows it.

stage.description: The stage the step is inside, named as the `stage` line behind this one names it (a stage's own name, `initflow`'s vocabulary). A step line a consumer cannot place in a stage is a step line it cannot draw.

name.description: The step itself. For a converge the two are the same string, because the stages are the steps; both are written so a consumer that reads a stage's progress by name has the member it expects wherever the CLI later has a step inside a stage that is not the stage.

detail.description: What the run has to say about the step while it is in flight, which is nothing until it settles: the `stage` line behind this one is where it speaks, so this is the empty string and not a member left out.

stage.description: One stage the run settled, with the members the `--json` document's `stages` element carries — so a consumer that read the document whole before the feed existed reads the same stage here, member for member, in the run's own stage order.

name.description: The stage, in `initflow`'s own vocabulary: the same string the document's `stages[].name` carries.

state.description: What the run settled the stage with: the document's own `stages[].state` word, unchanged (initflow's wire vocabulary — `initflow.State`). A run that left the stage for the user says `needs-you`, and the `left_for_you` line beside it is what says what is owed.
state.$comment: The members of initflow's State constants; setupStageEvent writes the string of that value.

detail.description: The stage's own one-line detail: the document's `stages[].detail`, unchanged — the plan's counts, the reason it was skipped, the sentence it failed with. A stage that reports `repos` says the summary those lines make instead ("3 repositories: 1 done, 1 needs you, 1 unread"), which is the same sentence from every directory, where a stage's own reason would name the directory it ran in; after that summary a stage that has one adds its own line about the step it did not run, naming the step and the repository it was dropped for ("1 repository: 1 unread; skipped here: acme/app: cloud (…)") — the summary counts how the repositories were left and never says which step was dropped for one of them.

after.description: The stage this one waited for, when it settled without doing its work because an earlier stage has to go first (`will-do` and `blocked` rows carry it); the empty string for a stage that waited for nothing.

undone.description: Whether the stage was skipped without doing its work, as opposed to one that found nothing to do: the document's `stages[].undone`, unchanged.

repos.description: The lines the stage reported about the repositories it read (C1's RepoLine, U13), in canonical owner/name order: one per repository it has something to say about, with how it left it. Always an array, and `[]` for a stage that reported none, so a consumer reads it without a case for "absent". The stage's own `detail` above is the summary these lines make, plus the line a stage has of its own where it has one, so what a consumer draws is the same from every directory. It is the same list the --json document's `stages[].repos` carries; a person reading the lines has them ordered with their working directory's repository first, which is the human output's alone.

repo.description: The repository's canonical owner/name, sanitised before it is written: it is repository-controlled text (C1's newRepoLine, R12).

state.description: How the stage left this repository (C1's RepoState): `done` for one it converged, `needs you` for one only its owner can take further, `unread` for one it could not read — its detail names the reason and the fix — and `skipped` for one the stage does not apply to.
state.$comment: The members of initflow's RepoState constants.

detail.description: One line a person reads about this repository, sanitised and bounded (C1's newRepoLine): absent for a line with nothing to say beyond its state.

left_for_you.description: One thing only the user can do: the document's own `left_for_you` entry, written the moment the run leaves it. It is what a surface reading the feed hands back to a person instead of waiting for one — the console's wizard lists every one of these and offers a Copy for a command — and it is why the feed needs no terminal: the run never waits for the step, it names it.

stage.description: The stage that left the step, in `initflow`'s own vocabulary: the document's `left_for_you[].stage`.

kind.description: How the user does what was left (initflow's LeftKind): a command to run, a prompt fugaro shows in a terminal, something done in a web console, or a step the managed gate refused — nothing written, and nothing the reader types or runs writes it.
kind.$comment: The members of initflow's LeftKind constants; setupLeftForYouEvent writes the string of that value.

text.description: The one sentence introducing the step, the document's `left_for_you[].text`: never a secret's value, and for a refused step the refusal itself.

commands.description: The complete lines to run, each one whole and in order — never joined by `&&` or `;` — the document's `left_for_you[].commands`. The array is always there and is `[]` for a step with no command (a console step, a refused one), so a consumer reads it without a case for "absent".
commands.$comment: setupEvents.left writes the empty array where initflow.Left.Commands is nil.

notice.description: One line the run reported outside its stages: a step after the stage loop (the fold, the pin, the budget mode), or an admit pattern the reader could not expand into repository names (R12, R19). It is the document's own `notices` entry, written where the run reported it, and it comes before the `done` or `error` line that ends the feed — the account the last line closes holds it.

step.description: The step that reported the line, in the run's own vocabulary. A step after the stage loop has no stage to report under, which is why its own name is here and not a `stage` name: the `notice` line is placed by nothing else. An admit pattern is reported by the step that read the list.

repo.description: The repository the line is about (its canonical owner/name), or the admit pattern the reader could not list (`github/acme/*`); the empty string for a notice about no repository at all. A repository's own text reaches it, so a consumer draws it as text.

state.description: How the step left it (C1's RepoState), or the empty string for a notice about no repository.
state.$comment: The members of initflow's RepoState constants, plus the empty string.

detail.description: The one line a person reads, sanitised by C1's newRepoLine before it was recorded (R12): a repository name or a provider's own sentence can reach it.

done.description: The last line of a feed whose run ended without failing. Its presence is the whole of it: a consumer that read lines and no `done` line is holding a read that was interrupted. A run that left steps for the user still ends here — the steps are the `left_for_you` lines above it, the exit code is 1, and the run did not fail: that is the hand-off a surface draws, and `error` is the other end.

exit_code.description: The code the process exits with, which is the number `--json`'s caller reads from the process (main's ExitCode over the command's own result): 0 for a run that converged, 1 for a refusal or a run with steps left for the user, 2 for a remote failure. It is written here so a consumer that reads only the feed has it, and it is the run's own and never the pipe's — a consumer that stopped reading changes nothing about the code.

error.description: The last line of a feed whose run stopped: the stage it stopped at, with the sentence and the fix the CLI printed, or — where the run refused before any stage — the refusal itself with `stage` and `fix` empty. There is no `done` line behind it, so a consumer reads the feed as stopped either way and this line is what says why.

stage.description: The stage the run stopped at, in `initflow`'s own vocabulary, or the empty string for a refusal that stopped the run before any stage ran (a flag the door does not take, a missing input). A run with steps left for the user is not a refusal and does not end here at all: its last line is `done` with exit 1.

error.description: The sentence the CLI printed, made safe for a terminal and for one line: a newline inside it would forge a second line of the feed, so it carries none. Text a remote service wrote can reach it, so a consumer classifies it as text and never as an instruction.

fix.description: The line the CLI tells the user to run to get past the failure (the failed stage's own fix), or the empty string where the run has none to give — a refusal.

exit_code.description: The code the process exits with, as on the `done` line: 1 for a refusal or a stopped run the user can act on, 2 for a remote failure.
